question.en: What is the difference between final and const in Dart?

keyPoints.en: Both prevent reassignment of the variable.
A final value is assigned once, possibly at runtime.
A const value must be known at compile time.

answer.en: Both final and const variables can be assigned only once. A final variable can get its value at runtime, for example from an API response. A const value must be known at compile time, and constant objects can be canonicalized.

followUp.en: Can a const object contain a field declared final?

commonMistake.en: Do not say that final and const mean exactly the same thing.

question.en: How does null safety help in Dart?

keyPoints.en: Types are non-nullable unless marked with a question mark.
Nullable values must be checked or handled.
Null safety catches many errors before runtime.

answer.en: In Dart, a type is non-nullable by default. I add a question mark when a value may be null, and then I must handle that case before using it as a non-null value. This helps catch many null errors during analysis instead of after release.

followUp.en: When is the null assertion operator reasonable to use?

commonMistake.en: Do not use the null assertion operator as a replacement for checking uncertain data.

question.en: When can a final variable receive its value?

options.en: Once, including from a value known only at runtime
Many times, as long as the new type stays unchanged
Only at compile time, before the program can run
Once per function call, when its scope is entered

why.en: A final variable is assigned once, and its value may be determined at runtime.

tip.en: Use const instead when the value is a compile-time constant.

question.en: How do you declare a Dart variable that may hold null?

options.en: Add a question mark to the type, such as String?
Add an exclamation mark to the type, such as String!
Wrap the type in braces, such as {String}
Use the dynamic keyword before the type name

why.en: The question mark makes the type nullable, so its value may be null.

tip.en: A nullable value needs handling before it is used as a non-null value.

question.en: What is a Dart record most useful for returning?

options.en: A fixed group of values with possibly different types
A growable collection of values with one shared type
A named class with custom methods and mutable fields
A key-value collection with runtime string lookups

why.en: Records group a fixed number of typed values without defining a new class.

tip.en: Record fields can be accessed by position or by declared name.

question.en: What does a Future<T> represent in Dart?

options.en: A value of type T that may become available later
A stream of type T values that continues over time
A synchronous result that is computed on another thread
A callback that must run before the current method returns

why.en: A Future represents one asynchronous result that will complete later.

tip.en: Use Stream when a source may emit multiple values over time.

question.en: A const variable's value must be known at compile time.

why.en: Dart requires const values to be compile-time constants.

tip.en: A final variable can instead be assigned from a runtime result.
